closures.observed_ui01_evidence: Production Nginx returned HTTP 200 at `/` with `<title>Laravel</title>` — the stock Laravel scaffold, which also loaded remote images from laravel.com. No working public Servana entry point was deployed at the root of any host.
closures.root_cause: `routes/web.php` bound `/` to `view('welcome')`, Laravel's untouched scaffold view. The SPA was never wired to the root; the only mount was Nginx's `/spa/` alias.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The scaffold is what the route returned, so no Nginx or Vite change could have altered the response body. Replacing the route is the smallest change that makes `/` Servana.
closures.correct_fix: Laravel renders the Servana SPA shell for every browser route on a resolved account host. `routes/web.php` binds a negative-lookahead path pattern to `SpaShellController`, guarded by `ResolveAccountHost`; `resources/views/spa.blade.php` is the shell; the stock `welcome.blade.php` was deleted.
tests: AccountHostShellContractTest::it serves the Servana shell — never the Laravel scaffold — on every account host
AccountHostShellContractTest::it keeps backend routes out of the SPA fallback
scripts/ui02-host-smoke.mjs (root status, title, no laravel.com reference)
closures.production_image_proof: servana-ui02-nginx:audit on port 8081 — all 8 hosts return 200 with `<title>Servana by Citrus</title>`, zero occurrences of the Laravel title or laravel.com assets.
closures.before: HTTP 200, `<title>Laravel</title>`, stock scaffold, remote laravel.com images.
closures.after: HTTP 200, `<title>Servana by Citrus</title>`, Servana shell carrying the resolved account key, `Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate`.
closures.remaining_risk: The shell is now rendered by PHP on every browser route rather than served as a static file. That is the standard Laravel+Vite arrangement and the cost is one PHP request per navigation, but it does mean an application-layer outage now also removes the shell. UI-17 owns production performance and resilience.

closures.observed_ui01_evidence: Vite emitted with `base: '/'` while Nginx mounted the SPA beneath `/spa/`. The shell requested `/assets/*`, those requests fell through to Laravel and returned HTML/404, and `/spa/` loaded an empty `#app`.
closures.root_cause: A path-ownership collision. Vite's default `assetsDir` is `assets`, and Laravel's own public tree already owns `public/assets` (brand files, landing images). One `/assets/` prefix therefore had two owners, and the Laravel front controller won — so every chunk resolved to Laravel's 404 HTML.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The chunks existed on disk at `public/spa/assets/*` and were reachable at `/spa/assets/*`; only the URL the shell asked for was wrong. Changing `base` alone would have moved the collision rather than removed it, because both owners still wanted the same prefix.
closures.correct_fix: One prefix per owner. Vite now emits to `spa-assets/` (`build.assetsDir`), Nginx serves `/spa-assets/` from `public/spa/spa-assets/` with immutable caching, and `/assets/` continues to serve Laravel's public tree. The shell names the fingerprinted entry from the real Vite manifest, so the two can never disagree.
tests: AccountHostShellContractTest::it names the fingerprinted Vite entry from the real manifest
closures.production_image_proof: servana-ui02-nginx:audit — entry JS 200 `application/javascript` with `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; entry CSS 200 `text/css`; on all 8 hosts.
closures.after: `/spa-assets/index-*.js` → 200 JavaScript, immutable; the SPA mounts and renders on all 8 hosts (asserted by the screenshot script's mount selector).
closures.remaining_risk: `/spa/` now 301s to the account root. A deep bookmark such as `/spa/dashboard` redirects to `/` rather than to `/dashboard`, which is a deliberate simplification — `/spa/` was never a product route and only ever served a blank page.

closures.observed_ui01_evidence: Nginx used `server_name _`, accepting any Host. No Laravel host resolver, route domain mapping or account-host registry existed. One origin served every account experience, and host context was not a governed runtime concept.
closures.root_cause: The eight-host architecture was adopted as a decision in UI-00 (ADR-016/ADR-017) but had no runtime. Nothing in the stack modelled 'which account is this request for'.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: Every downstream symptom — one shared landing surface, no per-account entry point, no unknown-host denial — follows from the absence of a host concept, not from any individual page.
closures.correct_fix: One canonical registry (`config/account-hosts.json`) with generated consumers: Laravel config, a typed frontend registry, and the Nginx `server_name` allowlist. `AccountHostResolver` performs exact-allowlist resolution with normalization and injection rejection; `ResolveAccountHost` denies unapproved hosts with a safe 421; Nginx's `default_server` returns 444; machine hosts are modelled in a separate server block.
tests: AccountHostResolutionTest (12 tests — production/local/staging maps, normalization, deceptive suffixes, injection, forwarded hosts, config cache)
closures.production_image_proof: servana-ui02-nginx:audit — 8 approved hosts resolve to their own account key; 4 unknown/deceptive hosts (attacker.test, evil-servana.ke, servana.ke.attacker.test, unknown.servana.test) are refused by connection close; the machine host serves /health 200 but / 404.
closures.before: `server_name _`; every Host accepted; no account concept anywhere in the runtime.
closures.after: 24 approved hosts (8 accounts x 3 environments) on an exact allowlist; unknown hosts closed at the edge; a typed account context resolved server-side and handed to the SPA; host context proven to grant nothing.
closures.remaining_risk: The registry currently derives staging hosts from a configured suffix with no DNS behind it. That is intentional — DNS, TLS and HSTS are UI-17 — but it means the staging map is unexercised against a real origin.

closures.observed_ui01_evidence: The preview origin did not own the Laravel public asset tree, so favicon URLs under `/assets/brand/*` failed wherever the SPA bundle was served as a separate root.
closures.root_cause: Two roots. The SPA bundle (`public/spa`) and Laravel's public tree (`public/`) were separate origins, and the shell referenced brand assets with root-absolute URLs that only one of them could satisfy.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The files were present and correctly named the whole time; only the origin serving the shell lacked them.
closures.correct_fix: In production Nginx serves `/assets/` from Laravel's public root — the authoritative copy — with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`. For parity on a standalone SPA origin (`vite preview`, which the Playwright harness uses), a build-time Vite plugin copies `public/assets` into the bundle from the same single source, so the two cannot drift.
tests: AccountHostShellContractTest::it references approved brand assets with canonical lowercase names
closures.production_image_proof: servana-ui02-nginx:audit — `/assets/brand/favicon.ico` 200, `/assets/brand/Logo.png` 200 on all 8 hosts; `/assets/brand/Logo.svg` 404 on all 8. A case-sensitive listing inside the image confirms `Logo.png` with its capital L.
closures.before: `/assets/brand/*` 404 on an origin that served only the SPA bundle.
closures.after: Favicons and Logo.png resolve at stable canonical-case URLs on every approved host; Logo.svg remains absent as the product owner directed.
closures.remaining_risk: The brand tree is now duplicated into the SPA build output for preview parity. It is copied at build time from the one source and `emptyOutDir` clears it each build, so it cannot go stale — but a future phase must not start treating the copy as authoritative.

explicitly_left_open.reason: The Playwright suite still runs against a Vite preview origin rather than the deployed one. UI-02 adds a focused production-origin host smoke; it does not take on the release-wide deployed-origin browser gate.
Role resolution belongs to the authentication and session phase.

newly_observed_not_owned_by_ui02.observation: An HTML-accept (browser-navigation) request to an auth-protected /api/v1 route returns 500 instead of a redirect, because Laravel's Authenticate middleware resolves `route('login')`, which has never existed.
newly_observed_not_owned_by_ui02.evidence: `git show origin/main:routes/web.php` contains no `login` route; the same code path existed before this phase. With `Accept: application/json` — the header the SPA always sends — the same endpoint correctly returns 401.
newly_observed_not_owned_by_ui02.action_taken: Recorded only. Not fixed, not closed, and not added to the UI-01 register, which is a historical snapshot.
